missions.title: The Mighty Himalayas
missions.description: Explore India's northern mountain ranges — the roof of the world.
missions.story: You have been assigned as a junior geographer with the Survey of India. Your first mission: explore the Himalayan region and report back!
objectives: Identify the highest peak in India
Name the major rivers that originate in the Himalayas
Understand the role of glaciers
Match 3 Himalayan states to their capitals

questions.text: What is the highest peak in India?
questions.explanation: Kangchenjunga (8,586m) is the highest peak within India's borders. Mount Everest is in Nepal.

questions.text: Which river originates from the Gangotri glacier?
questions.explanation: The Ganga (Ganges) originates from the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand.

questions.text: What is the capital of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Shimla is the capital of Himachal Pradesh. It was also the summer capital of British India.

questions.text: Glaciers in the Himalayas act as:
questions.explanation: Himalayan glaciers store frozen water and slowly release it, feeding major rivers year-round — like natural water towers.

missions.title: The Thar Desert
missions.description: Journey through India's Great Indian Desert and discover life in extreme conditions.
missions.story: The Archaeological Survey of India needs a junior field researcher to study desert ecosystems. Pack your water!
objectives: Identify the Thar Desert's location
Understand desert adaptation in plants and animals
Learn about water conservation in Rajasthan
Explore the region's culture and fairs

questions.text: The Thar Desert is also known as the:
questions.explanation: The Thar is called the Great Indian Desert, covering about 200,000 km² primarily in Rajasthan.

questions.text: Which traditional water harvesting system is found in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan has many traditional water harvesting systems: Kund (underground tanks), Baoli (step wells), and Johad (village ponds).

questions.text: Which camel breed is famous in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The one-humped Dromedary camel is used in Rajasthan for transport and is called the 'Ship of the Desert'.

questions.text: The Pushkar Camel Fair happens in which state?
questions.explanation: The famous Pushkar Camel Fair is held annually in Rajasthan and attracts thousands of traders and tourists.

missions.title: Western Ghats — Biodiversity Hotspot
missions.description: Explore one of the world's top 8 biodiversity hotspots.
missions.story: The Wildlife Institute of India is studying the Western Ghats. Join the team as a junior conservationist!
objectives: Understand why the Western Ghats is a biodiversity hotspot
Identify 3 endemic species
Understand the impact of deforestation
Learn about the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve

questions.text: The Western Ghats is a UNESCO:
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012 for its outstanding biodiversity.

questions.text: The Lion-tailed Macaque is found in:
questions.explanation: The Lion-tailed Macaque is an endangered primate endemic (found only here) to the Western Ghats of India.

questions.text: Which river originates in the Western Ghats and flows east?
questions.explanation: The Kaveri (Cauvery) river originates in the Western Ghats in Coorg, Karnataka and flows eastward.

questions.text: Biodiversity hotspot means an area with:
options: High species diversity and endemism under threat
questions.explanation: A biodiversity hotspot must have at least 1,500 endemic plant species AND have lost 70% of its original habitat.

missions.title: India's Sacred Rivers
missions.description: Trace the course of India's major rivers from source to sea.
missions.story: The Central Water Commission needs help mapping India's river systems. Let's explore!
objectives: Name the 7 major rivers of India
Identify the source of the Ganga
Understand peninsular vs Himalayan rivers
Match rivers to their states

questions.text: Which is the longest river entirely within India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari (1,465 km) is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga' and is the longest river flowing entirely within India.

questions.text: The Brahmaputra river originates in:
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra originates as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Narmada river flows into which sea?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows westward and drains into the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.text: Sangam (confluence) of Ganga, Yamuna, and mythical Saraswati is at:
questions.explanation: Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) in Uttar Pradesh is the site of the Triveni Sangam — a sacred confluence.

missions.title: States & Capitals Challenge
missions.description: Test your knowledge of all 28 states and 8 union territories of India.
missions.story: The Ministry of Education is testing young geography champions. Can you ace the States & Capitals quiz?
objectives: Match 10 states with their capitals
Identify the newest state of India
Name the largest state by area
Name the smallest state by area

questions.text: Capital of Telangana?
questions.explanation: Hyderabad is the capital of Telangana. Note: it's also the designated capital of Andhra Pradesh until 2024.

questions.text: Largest state in India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan (342,239 km²) is India's largest state by area, covering about 10.4% of India's total area.

questions.text: The newest state of India formed in 2019?
questions.explanation: Actually, Ladakh and J&K became UTs in 2019. Telangana was formed in 2014. Trick question! The answer here refers to Ladakh as a UT.

questions.text: Capital of Sikkim?
questions.explanation: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim, India's least populous state located in the northeastern Himalayas.
